options.text: Something that will definitely happen to the business
A potential problem that could negatively affect the business

questions.explanation: A business risk or challenge is a potential problem that could hurt the business — such as losing customers, running out of money, or supply chain issues. Start-ups face many risks.

questions.stem: A business opportunity is a chance to grow or improve the business.
questions.explanation: An opportunity is a favourable circumstance the business could take advantage of — such as a gap in the market, a growing trend, new technology, or a partnership. Identifying opportunities helps a business plan for growth.

questions.stem: What is a 'strategy' for dealing with a business challenge?

options.text: Ignoring the problem and hoping it goes away
A specific plan of action to reduce or manage the risk

questions.explanation: A strategy is a specific, practical plan to address the challenge. It should explain what the business would actually DO — not just acknowledge the problem exists.
questions.textbookRef: See pages 90–100 on risk management strategies

questions.stem: Classify each as a challenge or an opportunity.

pairs.left: A new competitor enters the market

questions.explanation: Challenges threaten the business (competition, rising costs). Opportunities offer growth potential (market trends, unmet demand). Good planning addresses both.
questions.textbookRef: See pages 90–100 on risks and opportunities

questions.stem: 'We will deal with it' is a good enough strategy for a business challenge.
questions.explanation: A strategy must be specific and actionable. 'We will deal with it' says nothing about what the business would actually do. A good strategy names concrete actions — like adjusting prices, finding new suppliers, or increasing marketing.
questions.textbookRef: See pages 90–100 on risk management strategies

questions.stem: If there is a growing trend of people wanting local, handmade products, what would be a good strategy to take advantage of this opportunity?

options.text: Ignore the trend and keep doing the same thing
Emphasise 'locally made' and 'handcrafted' in marketing to attract these customers
Raise prices as high as possible

questions.explanation: To take advantage of an opportunity, your strategy should connect your existing strengths to the trend. If people want local handmade products and you make them, highlighting that in your marketing is a practical, specific strategy.

questions.stem: Which is a realistic challenge for a NEW start-up business?

options.text: Having too many loyal customers from day one
Building brand awareness when no one knows your business yet
Having too much money to invest

questions.explanation: New businesses face the challenge of being unknown. Building brand awareness takes time and money. This is a realistic, specific challenge relevant to start-ups — unlike options that assume existing success.

questions.stem: An opportunity must be connected to something the business can actually act on.
questions.explanation: An opportunity is only useful if the business can realistically take advantage of it. A growing market for electric cars is not relevant to a bakery. The opportunity must connect to what your business does.
